reason: The battery fixes the power cut, but the water is my bigger problem. Many days the tank is not full or the motor cannot run, so the machine still sits idle and the women go back to washing by hand. ₹1,999 a month is not the issue for me, but I will not pay for something that solves only half the trouble.
objection: If the water is not there when the power is there, what good is a battery? I also do not know how long this lithium battery really lasts in our heat, and if it fails after three years the replacement will cost a lot.
would_change_my_mind: The dealer showing it working in a house like mine, filled by bucket from stored water with little water per load, and telling me the battery replacement price up front.
